title: Coriqo agent assurance benchmark result, format version 1
description: What one machine got when it ran a corpus through the validators. Carries no timestamp, no hostname and no run id, so two machines running the same corpus with the same validator versions produce byte-identical documents — reproducibility is the only thing that makes a published score checkable by someone who does not trust the publisher.

corpus_sha256.description: sha256 over the corpus file's bytes exactly as read. A result quoting a corpus_version whose bytes differ from the published corpus is a result against a modified corpus, and this field is how a reader tells.

sdk_version.description: Version of the coriqo-agents package that produced this document.

validator_versions.description: validator_id -> the version of the validator logic that ran. A score is only comparable against another score with the same versions here.

observed.description: Whatever status the validator actually returned, copied through unchanged — including a status this format does not know about. Deliberately not an enum: rewriting an unrecognised status into a recognised one is the failure this format exists to prevent.

outcome.description: `unevaluated` when `observed` is not one of the four comparable statuses (ERROR, INCONCLUSIVE, or anything this format version has never heard of). An unevaluated check is never a match and never enters the score's denominator.

score.description: `scored` is matched + mismatched. `ratio` is matched / scored, or null when scored is zero — a run where nothing could be evaluated has no score, and must never read as a perfect one.

unevaluated.description: Repeated here, not only in `totals`, so a consumer that renders the score cannot render it without the count of checks it excludes.
